labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

S59.01.needs: a Free account or a paid account that can use tools
steps: Sign in with an account that can run tools, open a chat, and send a request that needs a tool (for example a web search or a file write).
When the tool card shows 'This tool requires approval before execution.', read the card.
Click Allow (or Deny) on that one card.
Look at whether the tool ran (Allowed or Denied shown) and whether the reply continued, and compare with Expected.
S59.01.where: Chat > send a message that makes the agent use a tool that needs approval > on the tool card, click Allow or Deny

S59.02.needs: two or more pending tool calls in one run
S59.02.note: Tasks page (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TasksPage.tsx) has Approve and deny actions per run, not per call; the code does not show several calls approved in one click. Each request in the Approvals popover has its own Approve and Deny.

S59.03.needs: a Free account or a paid account that can use tools
S59.03.note: The UI says 'Allow for this chat' and the code scopes it to the conversation; Expected says 'rest of the current session'. Check the wording against the code.
steps: Open a chat and send a request that makes the agent use the same tool, such as a web search.
On the approval card, click Allow for this chat (this button is not shown for high-risk requests).
Send another request that uses the same tool in the same chat.
Check that it runs without asking again, and compare with Expected. Note it applies to this chat only, not the whole session.
S59.03.where: Chat > send a request that needs a tool > on the tool card, click Allow for this chat

labels.text: Control which tools this connector can run automatically.

S59.04.needs: a connected app (connector) on the account
S59.04.note: The exact path to the Connectors page label was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Open the Connectors page and choose a connected app.
In its tool permissions panel, find a tool and change its level (allow, ask or deny).
Use a chat request that calls that tool.
Check the tool follows the level you chose, and compare with Expected.
S59.04.where: Connectors > choose a connector > tool permissions panel (heading text 'Control which tools this connector can run automatically.')

S59.06.needs: a workspace admin account in a workspace
S59.06.note: The workspace console path label was not confirmed; the buttons are only enabled for admins.
steps: Sign in as a workspace admin and open the workspace console.
In the web domain section, type a site such as example.com into the site field.
Click Allow site or Block site, then check that the site appears under Allowed sites or Blocked sites.
Run a web search that should reach that site, and compare the result with Expected.
S59.06.where: Workspace console (organization settings) > web domain policy section ('Allow site' and 'Block site' buttons)

S59.07.needs: a signed-in account and a second device for the cross-device check
S59.07.note: The Settings tab label that opens the Capabilities section was not found in the code.
steps: Open Settings and go to the section that holds Tool approvals (the Capabilities section).
Choose a different option in the Default approval for tool actions group.
Sign out, or open the app on a second device signed in with the same account.
Check the chosen option is still selected, and compare with Expected.
S59.07.where: Settings > Capabilities > Tool approvals (radio group 'Default approval for tool actions')

S59.08.needs: a signed-in account; 'Skip approvals' may be disabled when the workspace requires asking every action
steps: Open Settings and go to Tool approvals in the Capabilities section.
Choose one of the three options: 'Ask before every action', 'Run read-only actions without asking', or 'Skip approvals'.
Run a read action and a write action in a chat.
Check that each one behaves as the chosen mode says, and compare with Expected.
S59.08.where: Settings > Capabilities > Tool approvals (radio group 'Default approval for tool actions')

S59.09.needs: a Free account or a paid account
S59.09.note: No read-only mode that refuses write, send and execute tools was found in the UI. The closest option, 'Run read-only actions without asking', still asks before writes. Searched the settings panels and tool-approval-policy.ts for a read-only refusal option.

S59.10.needs: a signed-in account that can use tools
steps: Open Settings, go to Tool approvals, and choose 'Run read-only actions without asking'.
In a chat, ask for a read action such as a web search; it should run without a card.
Ask for a write or send action; an approval card should appear.
Check reads ran on their own and writes stopped for approval, and compare with Expected.
S59.10.where: Settings > Capabilities > Tool approvals > 'Run read-only actions without asking'

S59.11.needs: a signed-in account that can use tools
S59.11.note: The UI calls this option 'Run read-only actions without asking'; there is no separate low-risk mode.
steps: Open Settings, go to Tool approvals, and choose 'Run read-only actions without asking'.
Ask for a search or page read in a chat and confirm it runs without a card.
Ask for an action that changes something and confirm an approval card appears.
Compare with Expected. The option is the same one used for S59.10.
S59.11.where: Settings > Capabilities > Tool approvals > 'Run read-only actions without asking'

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

S59.12.note: The page does not show a separate reason line; the code only shows the tool name and label.
steps: Send a request that needs an approval.
Click the Approvals button in the top bar, or look at the approval card in the conversation.
Read the title, the Request block and the line 'This tool requires approval before execution.'
Check the summary says what the tool will do and why it asks, and compare with Expected.
S59.12.where: Top bar of the chat > 'Approvals' button > a request card; the tool card in the conversation shows the same summary

S59.13.needs: a send-type tool connected to the account
S59.13.note: The detail row label text was not read; the rows come from the approval stakes code, so confirm the words on screen.
steps: Ask the agent to send a message to a named person.
Wait for the approval card to appear in the conversation.
Read the detail rows on the card and the Request block.
Check that the recipients are named before you approve, and compare with Expected.
S59.13.where: Chat > a request that sends a message or email > on the approval card, read the Request and detail rows

S59.14.needs: a request that reaches an outside site
S59.14.note: The destination row words were not read directly.
steps: Ask the agent to fetch a web page or send data to an outside site.
Wait for the approval card.
Read the detail rows for the destination (URL or host).
Check the destination shows before you approve, and compare with Expected.
S59.14.where: Chat > a request that opens or sends to an outside destination > on the approval card, read the detail rows

S59.15.needs: a purchase-capable tool connected to the account
S59.15.note: The approval stakes code has a purchase entry, but no purchase tool was found to test it. The exact wording on screen was not read.

steps: Ask the agent to run a command such as listing files in a folder.
Wait for the approval card.
Read the Request block, which shows the command text.
Check the exact command line is shown before you approve, and compare with Expected.
S59.16.where: Chat > a request that runs a command > on the approval card, read the Request block

steps: Ask the agent to create or change a file.
Wait for the approval card.
Read the detail rows and the Request block for the file or record names.
Check that the exact files or records are named before you approve, and compare with Expected.
S59.17.where: Chat > a request that writes a file > on the approval card, read the detail rows and the Request block

S59.18.note: The diff shows only when the tool request contains a file diff.
steps: Ask the agent to change text in a file.
Wait for the approval card.
Look in the Request block for the proposed diff lines.
Check the proposed change is visible before you approve, and compare with Expected.
S59.18.where: Chat > a request that edits a file > on the approval card, read the Request block (diff view)

steps: Send a request that needs approval.
When the approval card appears, click Allow.
Watch the tool card change state and the run continue.
Check the action ran and the card shows its result, and compare with Expected.
S59.19.where: Chat > send a request that needs a tool > on the approval card, click Allow

steps: Send a request that needs approval.
When the approval card appears, click Deny.
Check the card shows 'Denied' and the action did not run.
Ask the agent what happened; it should say the action was denied, and compare with Expected.
S59.20.where: Chat > send a request that needs a tool > on the approval card, click Deny

labels.text: Add guidance to steer the run (optional)

S59.22.note: The guidance box is in the Approvals popover, not on the tool card.
steps: Send a request that needs approval.
Click the Approvals button, then type guidance such as 'use a different site instead' in the box.
Click Deny (or Approve) for that request.
Check the agent continues with your guidance in the same chat, and compare with Expected.
S59.22.where: Top bar > 'Approvals' button > a request > text box 'Add guidance to steer the run (optional)', then Approve or Deny

labels.text: This approval request expired or is no longer active.
This request expired. Open the conversation to rerun the turn.

S59.23.needs: a request that needs approval, and patience for the time limit
S59.23.note: The time limit length was not found in the UI text.
steps: Send a request that needs approval and do not answer it.
Wait for the time limit to pass (the length is not shown in the UI).
Check the card shows the expired message and has no Allow button.
Try to use the old card; the action should not run, and compare with Expected.
S59.23.where: Chat > a request that needs approval > leave it waiting until it expires; the card then shows 'This approval request expired or is no longer active.'

S59.24.needs: a signed-in account with past approvals
S59.24.note: The Settings tab label that opens Capabilities was not found in the code.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Capabilities section.
Find the 'Approval history' heading.
Read the list, which shows requests you allowed or denied in chats, newest first.
Compare the list with the decisions you made earlier, and compare with Expected.

S59.25.needs: a connected app with saved permission choices
S59.25.note: The code resets all choices for the connector; a single saved 'always allow' revoke was not found.
steps: Open the Connectors page and choose a connected app with saved allow or deny choices.
Click Reset all to default.
Read the confirmation and click Reset permissions.
Use a chat request that calls the tool, and check it asks again, and compare with Expected.
S59.25.where: Connectors > choose a connector > tool permissions panel > 'Reset all to default' > 'Reset permissions'

S59.26.needs: two signed-in devices with the same account, plus a desktop app
S59.26.note: The sidebar label that opens the Tasks page was not confirmed.
steps: Start a task on one device that needs an approval (the desktop app).
Sign in with the same account on a second device and open the same run.
Approve the request on the second device.
Check the first device shows the result, and compare with Expected.
S59.26.where: Tasks page (run list) > a run waiting for approval; or the card text 'Waiting for [device]. Open the desktop app to continue.'

labels.text: High risk. Check the request below before you

S59.28.needs: a request that triggers a high-risk approval
S59.28.note: High-risk notice text is cut off in the code search; the full notice text is in tool-approval-policy.ts (TOOL_APPROVAL_HIGH_RISK_NOTICE).
steps: Send a request that is risky, such as one that could send private data outside.
Wait for the approval card.
Read the red notice at the top of the card and check that 'Allow for this chat' is not shown.
Click Allow only if you mean it, and compare with Expected.
S59.28.where: Chat > a sensitive request that needs approval > the approval card shows a high-risk notice and no 'Allow for this chat' button

labels.text: This tool requires approval before execution.

S59.30.needs: a paid account or a Free account that can reach a tool needing approval
S59.30.note: The code covers resuming after Allow or Deny only. I found no separate screen for resuming after answering a question or handing control back, so those parts of Expected are unverified.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a request that makes the assistant use a tool needing approval, for example a web action or a connector action.
When the tool card shows 'This tool requires approval before execution.', click Allow.
Watch the same assistant message: the run should carry on in that message after the click, and the tool card should show its result.
Compare with Expected: the run continues from where it stopped after the approval, with no new message started by hand.
S59.30.where: Chat > send a message that makes the assistant use a tool that needs approval > the tool card shows the text 'This tool requires approval before execution.' > click Allow (or Deny)

S59.31.needs: a paid account or a Free account that can reach a tool needing approval
S59.31.note: The denied count and step text are from the timeline and translation file; the exact wording for a successful run is shown in the card's result block, which I did not confirm in a rendered screen.
steps: Trigger a tool that needs approval in a chat (see S59.30).
Click Deny on the tool card and wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the tool step in the transcript: it should say the call was denied, using the count line 'You denied {count} tool call' and the 'denied' counter next to the step.
Click Allow on a second tool request, then look at its card: the result block should show what ran, or the error text if it failed.
Compare with Expected: the transcript shows what was decided and what happened (ran, result, or denied).
S59.31.where: Chat > after Allow or Deny on a tool card > look at the tool step in the same assistant message (count line 'You denied 1 tool call' or 'N denied')
